title: Orientation in Stages
transcript: When exchange students were asked what they remembered from their first morning at a university abroad, many could describe the welcome speech but few knew where to get help with their course registration. The international office had covered registration in the same long session as library rules, health services, and weekend activities. Staff replaced much of the session with short visits in small groups. At each stop, students completed one task, such as finding their academic adviser on the registration site. The office also sent reminders shortly before common deadlines. During the next intake, fewer students missed the deadline for changing courses. Questions about health services still came in several weeks later, so staff arranged a brief visit to the campus clinic after students had settled into their classes.

questions.prompt: What did students do during the new small-group visits?
options: They compared timetables with returning students.
They took turns giving short welcome speeches.
They completed one practical task at each stop.
They wrote a list of topics for a later lecture.
questions.answer: They completed one practical task at each stop.
questions.explanation: 每到一个地点，学生都要完成一项实际任务，例如在注册网站上找到学业导师。

questions.prompt: What does the timing of the clinic visit suggest about orientation?
options: Health information is easier to deliver through a registration website.
Some guidance may be more useful after students have settled in.
Students tend to seek health advice before classes begin.
Clinic visits are best combined with course registration.
questions.answer: Some guidance may be more useful after students have settled in.
questions.explanation: 健康服务的问题在几周后仍有人询问，校方因此把诊所参观安排在学生适应课程之后。
